structure: Part 18, "Document scan status and the client-side enhancements", read the whole of the animals frontend's document scan layer and the browser JavaScript over the Upload documents page, in repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend on main at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/. Read in full: scan/status.js and scan/summary-errors.js (the two non-test files under scan/); scan-poll.js (the status vocabulary, poll interval, attempt cap and poll decision shared by server and browser); download-content-type.js; client/index.js, client/dom.js, client/restored-page.js, client/scan-status/{page.js,poll.js,status-cell.js,announce.js} and client/oversize-validation/{submit.js,control.js,error-summary.js,field-error.js,markers.js} (every non-test file under client/); fit/scan-status.fit.spec.js (4 tests in 2 describes) and fit/drop-zone.fit.spec.js (6 tests); and copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js, from which only the keys this layer uses are claimed. The *.test.js unit tests beside these files were left unread, as the part says. To name the status word, tag colour and announcement each scan state shows, and to say where the browser's hooks come from, this part also read view-model/fragments/status.js, the parts of template.njk that carry the client hooks (lines 15-17, 54-56, 107-120, 146-190), view-model/refresh.js, the MAX_FILE_SIZE and ALLOWED_TYPES block of upload-config.js, handlers/reads/download.js, the getStatus handler and the route list of controller.js (lines 173-180, 406-439) and the oversizeMessage row of form/errors.js; the documents page itself, its add form and its table are part 17's and are not claimed here. Covered: the three scan statuses and the seven tag presentations; the GET <page>/status route, what it returns, the 3-second interval, the 10-attempt cap and the three ways polling ends; the five screen-reader announcements verbatim; the no-JavaScript refresh link and the timeout hint; the status cell and actions cell the poll rebuilds; the rejected-document error summary; the govuk-frontend drop zone and its copy; the in-browser oversize check, its wording and the server check behind it; the back/forward-cache reopen; and the download content type. The fit proof of the oversize check itself lives in fit/upload.fit.spec.js, which is part 17's file and is not claimed here.

claims.statement: A document the service has uploaded is in exactly one of three scan states: complete, pending or rejected.
A document whose scan has completed shows the status "Check completed" in a green tag.
claims.note: copy.scanTags.complete is 'Check completed'.

claims.statement: A document still being scanned shows the status "Scanning for virus" in a blue tag.
claims.quote: PENDING: { text: copy.scanTags.scanning, classes: 'govuk-tag--blue' }
claims.note: copy.scanTags.scanning is 'Scanning for virus'.

claims.statement: A document the upload service rejected for a reason the page has no wording for shows the status "Rejected" in a red tag.

...

claims.statement: A document rejected because the file contains a virus shows the status "Virus found" in a red tag.

claims.statement: A document rejected because the file could not be uploaded shows the status "Upload failed" in a red tag.
claims.note: copy.scanTags.uploadFailed is 'Upload failed'.

claims.statement: A document rejected because the file could not be downloaded shows the status "Download failed" in a red tag.
claims.note: copy.scanTags.downloadFailed is 'Download failed'.

claims.statement: A document whose scan state the page has no tag for shows the status "Unknown" in a grey tag.
claims.note: copy.scanTags.unknown is 'Unknown'.

claims.statement: Which status a rejected document shows is chosen by the reason the upload service gave, falling back to the plain rejection wording when the page has no wording for that reason.
claims.note: mechanism: maps a backend scan result (status plus rejection reason) to the tag key the status cell shows.

claims.statement: Every status tag is preceded by a visually hidden label reading "Virus check status for" and the document's reference, so a screen-reader user hears which document a status belongs to.
claims.note: copy.scanStatusHidden is `Virus check status for ${reference}`.

claims.statement: A document row that holds no uploaded file is treated as having a completed scan, so it shows no scanning status.
When the service cannot read a document's scan status it shows the document as still being scanned rather than failing the page.
claims.note: The failure is logged at warn with the journey id and upload id.

claims.statement: The page reads each uploaded document's scan status from the document upload service, passing the document's file name with the upload identifier.
The page asks for each document's scan status under its own path with "/status" on the end.

...

claims.statement: The scan-status request answers with a list of the notification's uploaded documents, each as its upload identifier, its scan status and the status wording key it should show.
claims.note: mechanism: documents with no upload identifier are left out of the answer.

claims.statement: Each scan-status request re-reads every document's status from the upload service rather than using a cached one.
The browser asks for the scan statuses every 3 seconds, starting 3 seconds after the page opens.
claims.quote:
export const POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 3000
...

claims.statement: The browser asks for the scan statuses at most 10 times.
claims.quote:
export const MAX_POLL_ATTEMPTS = 10
...
const lastAttempt = (attempt) => attempt + 1 >= MAX_POLL_ATTEMPTS

claims.statement: Asking stops as soon as no document is still being scanned.
Once every scan has settled the browser opens the documents page again so the page is rebuilt with the settled statuses, the Continue state and any rejection errors.
A request for the scan statuses that fails, is refused or answers with something unusable counts as one of the 10 attempts and the browser tries again after the interval.
When the 10 attempts run out with a document still being scanned, the page shows the hint "Still checking some documents. Refresh again in a moment."
claims.note: copy.stillChecking is 'Still checking some documents. Refresh again in a moment.'

claims.statement: The still-checking hint is rendered by the server on every load of the page and is hidden unless the page has already been refreshed 10 times with a document still scanning.
claims.quote:
{{ copy.stillChecking }}

claims.statement: Without JavaScript the documents page offers a "Refresh virus scan status" link whenever a document is still being scanned, so a trader can see the scan finish.
claims.note: copy.refreshStatus is 'Refresh virus scan status'.

claims.statement: When the browser starts asking for statuses itself, the "Refresh virus scan status" link is hidden, so only one way of refreshing is offered at a time.
The browser starts asking for statuses only when the page shows at least one document still being scanned.
The refresh link and the page the browser returns to carry a count of how many refreshes have happened, so the service knows when to show the still-checking hint.
claims.note: mechanism: an unreadable count is read as nought, and the refresh href also carries the handle of an open upload session so a part-filled add form is not lost.

claims.statement: Status announcements are made through one visually hidden polite live region at the foot of the page that is read out whole each time it changes.
Entering the scanning state announces nothing, because only settled states carry an announcement.
claims.note: Follows because the pending presentation has no announcement property and announce() does nothing without a message.

claims.statement: A status is announced only when it has actually changed, so a repeated answer does not repeat the announcement.
The status wording, tag colour and announcement for every state are handed to the browser with the page, so a status that changes without a reload reads exactly as a server-rendered one does.
claims.note: mechanism: the browser reads the wording from the announcer's data attribute rather than holding its own copy.

claims.statement: When a scan settles the row's status tag is rewritten where it stands, keeping the rest of the row and the hidden document label as they were.
When a scan completes without a reload, the row gains a "View file" link beside its Remove button.
A document whose scan settles as rejected offers no "View file" link, only Remove.
The "View file" link a settled row gains carries a visually hidden suffix naming which document it is for, and opens the file under the documents page's own path.

claims.statement: The service can say whether any document on a notification was rejected by the scan, and list the rejected ones.
claims.quote:
export const isRejectedByScan = (item) =>
  item.scanStatus === SCAN_STATUS.REJECTED

export const hasRejectedDocuments = (documents) =>
  documents.some(isRejectedByScan)

export const rejectedScans = (documents) =>
  scanned(documents.filter(isRejectedByScan))
claims.note: mechanism: these are read by the documents page and by the check-your-answers refusal, which part 17 and the check-answers part claim.

claims.statement: Before a document is sent, the browser refuses a file bigger than the service's limit without posting it.
The file-size limit is 50MB, counted as 50,000,000 bytes.
claims.quote:

const BYTES_PER_MEGABYTE = 1_000_000
export const MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES = MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB * BYTES_PER_MEGABYTE
export const MAX_FILE_SIZE_LABEL = `${MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB}MB`

claims.statement: An uploaded document a trader views is served only under a content type the journey accepts for an upload, and anything else is served as plain bytes so the browser never renders it.
claims.note: mechanism: the content type is taken from the upload service's answer, cut at the first semicolon, trimmed and lower-cased before it is matched; the accepted set is PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, PNG, XLS and XLSX.

claims.statement: A document the trader downloads is sent with instructions to the browser not to guess its type.

export const fileResponse = (h, streamed) =>

    .header('Content-Type', resolveDownloadContentType(streamed.headers))

claims.note: mechanism: how a download's content type and presentation are chosen; claimed in general terms as the handling of uploaded files a trader fetches back.
